pr_body:
This change simplifies and reduces the amount of boilerplate
code needed to get a device emulator up and running, thus reducing excise work
to writing tests.

Due to the change in EMUL_DEFINE and other code. This is a breaking-change for emulators.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/39486


Recreation of https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/45445 due to recreating my fork (ugh I didn't realize it would make my pull-requests go dead).
pr_comments:
Had to create a new pull-request due to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/45445#issuecomment-1163779915.

Sorry folks.

Made changes in response to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/45445#discussion_r888376932
Did *not* make changes in response to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/45445#discussion_r888375548 as author considered it "Fine" for now. The change requested might belong in its own tiny [PR](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/47009).

> Can we remove the use of `label` from things like emul_get_binding(), espi_emul_register(), etc..

Would you suggest something closer to how devices work?

```
#define DEVICE_DT_NAME(node_id) \
	DT_PROP_OR(node_id, label, DT_NODE_FULL_NAME(node_id))
```
Just added https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/46818/commits/86603b60c23510173ecc55f6e86637136714a8b5 except for one tiny clang-format that was missed in a prior commit.

> Can we remove the use of `label` from things like emul_get_binding(), espi_emul_register(), etc..

Now using  DEVICE_DT_NAME(node_id)

@galak

So using just the `dev` pointer from `DEVICE_DT_GET()` makes a lot of sense in
the context of just developing within the Zephyr project itself.

However, downstream Zephyr developers still converting their legacy drivers to
the Zephyr device driver model that would like to test their drivers using
emulators in the meantime would have difficulty; **this is the case for
ChromiumOS** where we're still porting our drivers to the Zephyr model but we
extensively test them using Zephyr emulators.

In this case, downstream devs have a device node but may only have an
`EMUL_DEFINE()` for that device node and not an associated
`DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()`. Meaning `DEVICE_DT_GET()` would **not** resolve to a
defined address.

Using `DEVICE_DT_NAME()` lets us directly create a 1:1 correspondence between DT
node and emulator, but gives downstream developers the flexibility to test their
legacy drivers with their emulators as they migrate to the Zephyr device model
and upstream their drivers/emulators. Whereas using `DEVICE_DT_GET()` does not
allow for such flexibility as it requires `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()` to use an
associated emulator.

> @galak
> 
> So using just the `dev` pointer from `DEVICE_DT_GET()` makes a lot of sense in the context of just developing within the Zephyr project itself.
> 
> However, downstream Zephyr developers still converting their legacy drivers to the Zephyr device driver model that would like to test their drivers using emulators in the meantime would have difficulty; **this is the case for ChromiumOS** where we're still porting our drivers to the Zephyr model but we extensively test them using Zephyr emulators.
> 
> In this case, downstream devs have a device node but may only have an `EMUL_DEFINE()` for that device node and not an associated `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()`. Meaning `DEVICE_DT_GET()` would **not** resolve to a defined address.
> 
> Using `DEVICE_DT_NAME()` lets us directly create a 1:1 correspondence between DT node and emulator, but gives downstream developers the flexibility to test their legacy drivers with their emulators as they migrate to the Zephyr device model and upstream their drivers/emulators. Whereas using `DEVICE_DT_GET()` does not allow for such flexibility as it requires `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()` to use an associated emulator.

I'm not sure I get this.  `EMUL_DEFINE` already utilizes devicetree as it takes a `node_id` param.  So what are downstream users passing for that param?

> I'm not sure I get this. `EMUL_DEFINE` already utilizes devicetree as it takes
> a `node_id` param. So what are downstream users passing for that param?

So using `node_id` is completely fine. But the `const device *` pointer from
`DEVICE_DT_GET()` will not resolve to anything if there isn't also a
`DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()` call for the same `node_id`. However, `DEVICE_DT_NAME()`
will resolve as long as the `node_id` exists.

The specific case I'm discussing is:

There's a `node_id` in a codebase for a peripheral that has a legacy non-Zephyr
driver (this happens in ChromiumOS). Since the legacy driver isn't ported to
Zephyr device driver model yet, it has no `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()`. **But** we still
want to test the legacy driver using Zephyr emulators. In this case, using
`DEVICE_DT_GET()` in the `EMUL_DEFINE()` macro will break.

Let me know if you'd like to see a ChromiumOS example. We can also do a short
call via Discord or otherwise if you'd like.

> So using `node_id` is completely fine. But the `const device *` pointer from `DEVICE_DT_GET()` will not resolve to anything if there isn't also a `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()` call for the same `node_id`. However, `DEVICE_DT_NAME()` will resolve as long as the `node_id` exists.
> 
> The specific case I'm discussing is:
> 
> There's a `node_id` in a codebase for a peripheral that has a legacy non-Zephyr driver (this happens in ChromiumOS). Since the legacy driver isn't ported to Zephyr device driver model yet, it has no `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()`. **But** we still want to test the legacy driver using Zephyr emulators. In this case, using `DEVICE_DT_GET()` in the `EMUL_DEFINE()` macro will break.
> 
> Let me know if you'd like to see a ChromiumOS example. We can also do a short call via Discord or otherwise if you'd like.

But you are already breaking downstream drivers by changing `EMUL_DEFINE()`.  So not sure I see how its that difficult to change those drivers to use `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE` vs changing them to use this new version of `EMUL_DEFINE()`.  And if that is a burden, than change `EMUL_DEFINE` to take a dev pointer and we can put the burden on the caller.

@galak 

So after some further discussion with @yperess we're going to go with what you've suggested and use `DT_DEVICE_GET()` in place of the node name. I was concerned about stubbing out device structs downstream but it seems easy enough to just stub them out for emulators that don't have a corresponding `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()`. There's actually an example in this commit so we could get the espi_host tests passing.

I'd prefer to not add `node_id` as a parameter in the `EMUL_DEFINE` for now, but I have documented a required corresponding `DT_DEVICE_DEFINE()`.

Maybe having the stubbed out device structs will be a good reminder for us downstream folks to migrate our legacy drivers to the Zephyr model too :)

By the way, thank you for the time you've spent reviewing this PR!

> Is there any reason to keep `emul_get_binding` vs replacing it with a version that does the matching based on a `struct device`?

Just to keep it consistent with the device_get_binding signature. I don't feel particularly strong about this one, but @yperess does I believe.

> Just to keep it consistent with the device_get_binding signature. I don't feel particularly strong about this one, but @yperess does I believe.

@yperess I don't think it makes sense to propagate device_get_binding for emul.

@galak

Keeping name as the parameter for `emul_get_binding()` prevents a required
`device_get_binding()` beforehand which iterates over the devices. It isn't a
significant increase in time iterating, but if clients have to call
`device_get_binding()` for every `emul_get_binding()` it may slightly add up on
some future integration tests that make use of many emulators, which we
certainly have downstream. It's really just we'd have to iterate through all
devices each time when we could just be iterating on emulators.

Let me know if you still don't feel this is a good enough reason and I can make
a change, but this is the other significant reasoning for keeping
`emul_get_binding(name)`.

> @galak
> 
> Keeping name as the parameter for `emul_get_binding()` prevents a required `device_get_binding()` beforehand which iterates over the devices. It isn't a significant increase in time iterating, but if clients have to call `device_get_binding()` for every `emul_get_binding()` it may slightly add up on some future integration tests that make use of many emulators, which we certainly have downstream. It's really just we'd have to iterate through all devices each time when we could just be iterating on emulators.
> 
> Let me know if you still don't feel this is a good enough reason and I can make a change, but this is the other significant reasoning for keeping `emul_get_binding(name)`.

I'm not sure I follow the need to call `device_get_binding`.  We can deal with this in a follow up PR.  My main point is that doing name comparisons doesn't make sense to me when we have `struct device` pointers and we can just do pointer comparisons.  Less costly to compare a pointer than doing a string compare, and more robust to not depend on names.

comments: Can you please point to (or add here) an example node for the emulator? Originally the emulator did not have its own node. Has that changed?

review_comments: nit: formatting here looks odd.  the `.config...` seems like it should be on its own line.

This is from [a clang-format](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/.clang-format), I tried putting the `.config...` on its own line and `clang-format` just puts it back where it is now.
Why are you changing this perfectly formatted piece of code here (and on other places)? These changes are not necessary at all.

[Zephyr uses clang-format](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/.clang-format) to properly format code. My understanding is the project is working on making this more consistent and enforced on future changes.

Making code consistently formatted is necessary to improve readability and future diffs easier to parse.

So this change is certainly necessary. Are you suggesting it belongs in its own PR?

> Why are you changing this perfectly formatted piece of code here (and on other places)? These changes are not necessary at all.

It doesn't conform to the coding guidelines

No. From [Contribution Guidelines](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/contribute/guidelines.html#coding-style), "The [clang-format tool](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormat.html) can be helpful to quickly reformat large amounts of new source code". Is is not new code, most of the code is perfectly formatted. It conform to our coding style, which ->` In general, follow the [Linux kernel coding style](https://kernel.org/doc/html/latest/process/coding-style.html),` -> "The preferred limit on the length of a single line is 80 columns."

Then it looks like the Code Style section of the contribution guidelines doc is out-of-date. The [clang-format configuration change increasing the line length to 100](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/46952) strongly suggests this is the case since there's no sensible reason to have two different styles within the same project unless the project is slowly migrating to from one to the other; that is my understanding here.

[This was the last change to the contribution guidelines](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/c7e4388b1dc5a42f171b87af70d2c033b4d9b917) which happened before the `clang-format` config change, which probably should've happened in the [clang-format config change PR](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/46952).

Between the contribution guidelines or the clang-format configuration, I'd absolutely consider the clang-format configuration as the source of truth since docs grow stale.

As for applying `clang-format` to "new source code": here `clang-format` was only applied to files changed within this PR. It'd be quite tedious to only apply `clang-format` specifically to new code regions and this would make the code within a source file inconsistently formatted.

Requesting a review from @nashif to comment on this here.

None of this justifies the change to the perfectly formatted code. I do not see different styles, I see imperfection of clang-format. Also, our coding styles are not so complicated that an average contributor could not follow them. You have even existing code as a template that you just needed to follow.

There is nothing wrong about this change, it does follow the guidelines. 
"perfectly formatted code" is VERY subjective.

Marking this as resolved, @jfischer-no I understand your concern, but the issue here is that if files are formatted differently, then when the next developer is going in and making future changes they will first have to learn the style of the current file in order to match it. The alternative is to have sections of code with different formats (which I think all of us will agree is not acceptable). @aaronemassey 's approach here is reasonable, running clang-format in a separate commit first, then applying changes to make review easier.

No I strongly disagree. We do not refactor the code in the project that complies with coding style. clang-format reformatted code does not match our established style. And here currently you are enforcing different coding style.

> #30426

Well maximum length in checkpatch does not apply here (and coding-style is already quoted above). The issue is also how clang-format formats the parameters and arguments of a function. There will always be unnecessary changes, and so clang-format is not suited to do formatting without manual post-processing.

This should be:

```
#define EMUL_BUS_TYPE_I2C  UINT32_C(0)
#define EMUL_BUS_TYPE_ESPI UINT32_C(1)
#define EMUL_BUS_TYPE_SPI  UINT32_C(2)

/**
 * Vendor specific types should start here, example:
 * @code
 * #define MY_BUS_TYPE (EMUL_BUS_TYPE_VENDOR + UINT32_C(1))
 * @endcode
 */
#define EMUL_BUS_TYPE_VENDOR UINT32_C(3)
```

I don't want to hold off this change, but can you file an issue to modify this later?
